title: Walk-off mats and elevator door tracks
audience: Cleaners who service entrance mats in commercial and strata buildings and clean the door tracks of passenger lifts where the site allows.
learningOutcomes: Vacuum a walk-off mat using a set pass pattern so that the soil is drawn out from the full mat.
Describe the lock-out steps that must be in place before any work near lift doors and tracks.
Clean lift door tracks with the right tool and product, and stop if the lift cannot be made safe to work near.

instruction.heading: Walk-off mats collect most of the entrance soil
instruction.body: A walk-off mat at an entrance traps grit and moisture before it reaches the remainder of the building. If the mat is not vacuumed, the soil works its way into the floor covering beyond it. The mat should be vacuumed on a regular schedule, and its pattern of passes matters: a single pass leaves soil in the matting. A set number of passes in each direction, starting from the edge where people step on, draws the soil up from the full depth of the mat.

instruction.heading: The pass pattern for a walk-off mat
instruction.body: Use an upright or backpack vacuum. Begin at the edge people step onto and run ten strokes over the first three metres. Follow with five strokes lengthwise and five crosswise. Lift the mat and vacuum the floor beneath it too, since soil collects there.

instruction.heading: Lift doors and tracks: confirm lock-out before work
instruction.body: Lift door tracks are a place where fingers and tools can be caught when the doors move. Before any work near the doors, the lift must be taken out of service at the site's lock-out point, and the lift should not be called to that floor while work is in progress. Use the site's lock-out procedure and confirm it with the building contact. If the lock-out cannot be confirmed, do not start the work. Do not reach into the door gap, and do not work on the lift's motors, controls or door mechanism. Those are for the lift contractor.

instruction.heading: Cleaning the tracks
instruction.body: With the lift locked out, vacuum the track with a backpack hose and a crevice tool to remove dry grit. Apply an approved track cleaner suited to the metal or coating, work the grooves using the grout brush; wipe away residue with paper towel. Check that no residue is left in the groove. Do not spray cleaner into the door mechanism or the lift's electrical parts. When the track is dry, reinstate the lift according to the site's procedure and confirm it is working before you leave.

procedure: Put on gloves and eye protection before handling the mat or the track cleaner.
Choose an upright or backpack vacuum and set it up to the mat's size.
Roll the mat, and vacuum the first three metres from the entry edge with ten passes.
Vacuum the mat's length with five passes and its width with five passes.
Lift the mat to vacuum beneath it, then lay it back in position.
Confirm the lift lock-out is in place with the building contact before any work near the doors.
Vacuum the door track with a backpack hose and crevice tool to remove dry grit.
Apply an approved track cleaner, work the grooves using the grout brush; wipe away residue with paper towel.
Dry the track, check the grooves, and reinstate the lift according to the site's procedure before leaving.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner is asked to clean the lift tracks in a busy office building. The lift is still in service and the cleaner plans to work quickly between floors.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner do before starting?
workedExamples.reasoning: The lift must be locked out first and confirmed with the building contact. Working with the doors able to move exposes the hands and tools to a crush or pinch hazard. If the lock-out cannot be confirmed, the cleaner should not start, and should report that to the supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: A walk-off mat at a shop entrance has a clean surface, but the soil underneath is visibly built up when the cleaner rolls it up.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should be done, and how should future cleans change?
workedExamples.reasoning: Vacuum underneath the mat as part of every clean, not just the surface. Include the roll-up step in the routine so the soil does not build up beneath the matting.

equipmentAndPpe: Upright or backpack vacuum with a hose and crevice tool.
Approved track cleaner suited to the metal or coating, with its label and safety data sheet available.
Lock-out sign and the site's lock-out procedure.
Wet floor sign for the lobby or entrance.

commonErrors.error: Making one pass over a mat and calling it clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the full pass pattern: ten passes over the first three metres, then five each way.

commonErrors.error: Starting work on a lift track before the lock-out is in place and confirmed.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the lock-out with the building contact, and do not start if it cannot be confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Spraying cleaner into the door mechanism or the lift's electrical parts.
commonErrors.prevention: Spray only onto the cloth or brush for the track, and keep the product out of the mechanism.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Lift doors can move and cause crush or pinch injuries. Do not begin work near the doors until the lift is locked out and confirmed.

Licence notice: this lesson covers cleaning access around lift doors and tracks only, after lock-out. It does not cover work on lift motors, controls, door mechanisms or electrical parts, which should be left to the building's lift contractor. Completing this lesson does not grant any licence or authority to work on a lift.
Wet tracks and mats are slippery. Place signs at the entrance and clear the walkway before work.

qualityStandard: The mat has been vacuumed with the full pass pattern and underneath has been cleared.
The mat is returned to position, flat and without a trip edge.
The lift was confirmed locked out before any work started near the doors.
The track is free of visible grit and residue, and no product has reached the mechanism.
The lift has been reinstated according to the site's procedure.
documentationEvidence: Job record of the mat and track cleaned, with the date and time.
Record of the lift lock-out, the name of the building contact who confirmed it, and the time the lift was reinstated.
Note of any damage to a mat, door track or door mechanism, for the building contact.
summary: Clean entrance mats with the full pass pattern and clear soil from underneath.
Confirm the lift lock-out with the building contact before any work near the doors.
Clean tracks with a vacuum, an approved cleaner on a brush or cloth, and a grout brush for the grooves.
Leave mechanical and electrical parts to the lift contractor.

knowledgeChecks.question: How many passes should be made over the first three metres of a walk-off mat?
options: One pass over the whole mat, in one direction only at a steady pace
Ten passes over the first three metres, then five each way across the mat
Twenty passes over the centre of the mat only and then the edges

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be confirmed before any cleaning work starts near lift doors?
options: The lift is busy, so the cleaner can work quickly between floors
The lift door is open, so the track is easier to reach and the cleaner can reach in
The lift is locked out and the lock-out is confirmed with the building contact

knowledgeChecks.question: Which work on a lift is outside a cleaner's scope?
options: Work on the motors, controls, door mechanism or electrical parts
Vacuuming the track with a crevice tool after lock-out
Wiping the track with paper towel once it has dried
